source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 1–4.

key_decisions.decision: Retains the bodily sign and snow comparison without diagnosing the biblical skin-condition term as modern Hansen’s disease.
Retains the unusual voice-of-sign personification that connects believing and listening.
Keeps the temporal insistence and heavy-mouth/tongue idiom without diagnosing a particular impairment or making humility the only cause.
Preserves the difficult divine claim and all named capacities using respectful contemporary descriptions, without assigning blame to disabled people.
Renders the idiomatic send-by-whomever-you-will as Moses’ refusal while documenting the literal expression in a note.
Keeps divine anger, Aaron’s kinship and Levite description, emphatic speaking ability, and his anticipated joy.
Preserves the provocative God/mouth relationship as a functional comparison rather than calling Moses divine by nature.
Preserves the request’s stated reason rather than replacing it with the commission; uses Jethro for the short and full name forms within this verse.
Retains plural sons although only one has yet been named, the donkey, and the newly designated staff of God.
Preserves God’s first-person hardening and refusal sequence without attributing this action to Pharaoh instead.
Retains collective Israel as the specifically male firstborn image that governs the warning.
Preserves the direct killing warning, refusal, and repeated son/firstborn contrast without euphemism.
Leaves the unnamed threatened person as him rather than silently deciding between Moses and his son; retains the LORD as agent.
Keeps Zipporah’s action, flint, foreskin, ambiguous feet and pronoun, and the opaque blood-bridegroom phrase without inventing an explanation.
Retains the pronouns and circumcision explanation while leaving the precise ritual meaning unresolved.
Follows the continuing grammatical subject while noting the possible Moses referent for performed; no unsupported stage directions are added.
Preserves believed/heard order and attended/seen echoes of the promise and follows Hebrew heard rather than the ancient Greek rejoiced.
